rationale: N-Dynamic provides native pod routing without encapsulation and advertises pod CIDRs through per-node BGP peering to Cloud Router, allowing on-premises systems to reach pod IPs directly. It preserves the network team’s end-to-end routing control on the self-managed kubeadm cluster and avoids the operational and platform costs of migrating to GKE, while meeting the stated connectivity requirements.

N-Dynamic avoids encapsulation and provides direct pod-IP reachability through per-node BGP peering with Cloud Router, matching the network team’s routing-control requirements. It is appropriate for a self-managed kubeadm cluster, though the number of BGP sessions and Cloud Router resources should be sized for 200 nodes.

N-Dynamic provides direct pod-IP routing without encapsulation and uses per-node BGP peering with Cloud Router, matching the requirement for on-premises reachability and centralized routing control. It avoids GKE adoption and the operational limitations of static route updates, while keeping costs lower than migrating the workload to GKE, although 200 BGP sessions add management overhead.

It is more costly to operate than static routes, but N-Static does not meet the requirement for BGP-based routing control, while N-Cloud is incompatible with the self-managed kubeadm cluster.

It fits the self-managed kubeadm deployment and avoids the operational and compatibility constraints of VXLAN, while costing less than migrating to GKE with alias-IP native routing.
